name: 2nd Dan

practical.title: Choong-Jang
practical.detail: 52 movements. Named after General Kim Duk Ryang, who died in prison aged 27. Ends with a left-hand attack, then return to ready posture. Includes forearm and guarding blocks, finger and elbow thrusts, snap and turning kicks, knife-hand strikes, crescent and double punches, back-fist strikes.

practical.title: Eui-Am
practical.detail: 45 movements. Named after Son Byong Hi, a leader of the 1919 independence movement; 45 relates to his age when he renamed Dong Hak as Chondo Kyo in 1905. Includes X-fist and wedging blocks, twist and reverse turning kicks, back-fist and side strikes, palm blocks, punches. Ends with return to ready posture.

practical.title: Ko-dang
practical.detail: 39 movements. Named after the patriot Cho Man Sik; 39 relates to his imprisonments and his birthplace on the 39th parallel. Includes pushing and pressing palm blocks, forearm and knife-hand blocks, back piercing kicks, elbow thrusts, hooking kicks, cross cuts, jump X-stances. Ends with return to ready stance.
